items.stem: State what is meant by the term "byte".
items.answer: A group of 8 bits
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a group of 8 bits. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): 8 bits can store 256 different values.
Reason (R): The largest 8-bit unsigned number is 256.
Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
items.answer: A is true but R is false.
items.markingKey: C. A true; R false – the largest is 255.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why hexadecimal is used for colour codes and memory addresses.
items.answer: Each hex digit maps to exactly 4 bits, so long binary values (e.g. 24-bit colours, 32/64-bit addresses) become short, readable codes with less chance of transcription error. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Each hex digit maps to exactly 4 bits, so long binary values (e.g. 24-bit colours, 32/64-bit addresses) become short, readable codes with less chance of transcription error. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.) (3 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Add 01110100 and 00101110, which are 8-bit two's complement integers. Give the 8-bit result and state whether overflow has occurred.
items.answer: 10100010 (overflow – the true sum 162 is out of range)
items.markingKey: 116 + 46 = 162; 8-bit result 10100010 read as -94 (A1); overflow: yes because both operands have the same sign but the result sign differs (R1).

items.stem: Convert the binary number 11101001 to denary. Show your working.
The unsigned 8-bit value 00000111 is shifted logically 1 place to the right. State the result in binary and denary, and the arithmetic effect of the shift.
items.answer: 00000011 = 3; integer-divided by 2
items.markingKey: 00000011 (A1) = 3 (A1); a right shift by 1 divides (discarding the remainder) by 2^1 (R1).

items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "Hexadecimal is no longer needed now that programming languages are high level."
items.answer: Hex remains essential wherever bit patterns are shown to humans, though less common in everyday application coding.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: high-level code hides memory addresses and bit patterns; most developers rarely write binary directly. Arguments against: hex is still used for colour codes, MAC/IPv6 addresses, memory dumps and debugging; error codes and machine code are shown in hex. Supported judgement: Hex remains essential wherever bit patterns are shown to humans, though less common in everyday application coding.

items.stem:
(a) A student claims: "Hexadecimal saves memory because it uses fewer digits than binary." Identify the error in this claim and correct it. [2]
(b) Add 11000001 and 11011001, which are 8-bit two's complement integers. Give the 8-bit result and state whether overflow has occurred. [3]
(c) Evaluate the claim: "Hexadecimal is no longer needed now that programming languages are high level." [6]
items.answer: (a) Hex is only a human-readable notation; the computer stores the same binary bits regardless. (b) 10011010 (= -102, no overflow) (c) Hex remains essential wherever bit patterns are shown to humans, though less common in everyday application coding.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A single binary digit, 0 or 1 – the smallest unit of data"?
options: character set
NAND gate
bit
byte
items.answer: bit
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of bit.

items.stem: A student claims: "1 KB is always exactly 1000 bytes in every context." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Computing often uses binary prefixes: 1 KiB = 1024 bytes; SI kilobyte = 1000 bytes; the context must be stated.
items.markingKey: Computing often uses binary prefixes: 1 KiB = 1024 bytes; SI kilobyte = 1000 bytes; the context must be stated. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: The unsigned 8-bit value 00011011 is shifted logically 2 places to the right. State the result in binary and denary, and the arithmetic effect of the shift.
items.answer: 00000110 = 6; integer-divided by 4
items.markingKey: 00000110 (A1) = 6 (A1); a right shift by 2 divides (discarding the remainder) by 2^2 (R1).

items.stem: Show how −45 is represented in 8-bit two's complement, then add it to +100 in binary, explaining how the carry is handled and how to check whether overflow has occurred.
items.answer: +45 = 00101101; invert → 11010010; +1 → 11010011 = −45. 100 = 01100100. Sum: 01100100 + 11010011 = 1 00110111; discard carry out → 00110111 = 55 (correct). Overflow occurs only if two numbers with the same sign give a result with a different sign; here signs differ, so no overflow.
items.markingKey: +45 = 00101101; invert → 11010010; +1 → 11010011 = −45. 100 = 01100100. Sum: 01100100 + 11010011 = 1 00110111; discard carry out → 00110111 = 55 (correct). Overflow occurs only if two numbers with the same sign give a result with a different sign; here signs differ, so no overflow.

items.stem: The ASCII code for "A" is 65. What is the ASCII code for "E"?
items.markingKey: B. Letters are consecutive: A=65, B=66, … E=69.

items.stem: Explain the difference between colour depth and resolution.
items.answer: Resolution is the number of pixels in the image; colour depth is the number of bits used for the colour of each pixel. Both increase file size.
items.markingKey: Resolution is the number of pixels in the image; colour depth is the number of bits used for the colour of each pixel. Both increase file size. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why a higher sample rate produces a more accurate digital sound recording.
items.answer: Samples are taken more often, so the stored values follow the shape of the analogue wave more closely and higher frequencies can be captured (Nyquist: sample rate ≥ 2 × highest frequency). (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Samples are taken more often, so the stored values follow the shape of the analogue wave more closely and higher frequencies can be captured (Nyquist: sample rate ≥ 2 × highest frequency). (a) Define the term "ASCII". [2]
(b) Explain why a higher sample rate produces a more accurate digital sound recording. [2]
(c) A satellite thumbnail is 1920 × 1080 pixels with a colour depth of 4 bits. Calculate the file size in KiB, ignoring metadata. [3]
items.answer: (a) A 7-bit character set representing 128 characters: English letters, digits, punctuation and control codes (b) Samples are taken more often, so the stored values follow the shape of the analogue wave more closely and higher frequencies can be captured (Nyquist: sample rate ≥ 2 × highest frequency). (c) 1012.5 KiB

(c) [3 marks] 1920 × 1080 × 4 = 8,294,400 bits (M1); ÷ 8 = 1,036,800 bytes (M1); ÷ 1024 = 1012.5 KiB (A1).

items.stem:
Case study context: Harbour Health, a private clinic group in Auckland, stores patient records on a central server, lets doctors access them from tablets over Wi-Fi and must keep data confidential.
(a) Distinguish between colour depth and resolution. Refer to Harbour Health in your answer. [3]
(b) Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "UTF-8 is the best choice of encoding for every text file." Refer to Harbour Health in your answer. [3]
items.answer: (a) Resolution is the number of pixels in the image; colour depth is the number of bits used for the colour of each pixel. Both increase file size. (b) UTF-8 is the best default for interoperability, though UTF-16 can be more compact for some scripts.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "ASCII"?
options: The rules NOT (A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B and NOT (A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B
The base-16 number system using the digits 0-9 and A-F, where each hex digit represents exactly four bits
An error that occurs when the result of a calculation is too large to be stored in the available number of bits
A 7-bit character set representing 128 characters: English letters, digits, punctuation and control codes
items.answer: A 7-bit character set representing 128 characters: English letters, digits, punctuation and control codes
items.markingKey: D. "ASCII" is a 7-bit character set representing 128 characters: English letters, digits, punctuation and control codes.

items.stem: "A sound recorded at 44.1 kHz stores 44.1 samples per second." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: 44.1 kHz means 44 100 samples per second.

items.answer: 8 bytes in UTF-8; 24 bytes in UTF-32

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "truth table"?
options: A table listing every combination of inputs to a logic circuit and the corresponding output
The base-2 number system, which uses only the digits 0 and 1, each representing a power of 2
A character set that can represent over a million characters from all writing systems, encoded as UTF-8, UTF-16 or UTF-32
A gate whose output is 0 only when all inputs are 1 – the inverse of AND; any circuit can be built from NAND gates alone
items.answer: A table listing every combination of inputs to a logic circuit and the corresponding output
items.markingKey: A. "truth table" is a table listing every combination of inputs to a logic circuit and the corresponding output.

items.stem: Distinguish between an XOR gate and an OR gate.
items.answer: OR outputs 1 when one or both inputs are 1; XOR outputs 1 only when exactly one input is 1, so it gives 0 for (1,1).
items.markingKey: OR outputs 1 when one or both inputs are 1; XOR outputs 1 only when exactly one input is 1, so it gives 0 for (1,1). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why NAND gates are called universal gates.
items.answer: NOT, AND and OR can all be built from NAND gates alone (NOT A = A NAND A, etc.), and every Boolean function can be built from NOT, AND and OR, so any circuit can be made from NANDs only – simplifying manufacture. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)
items.markingKey: Award marks for: NOT, AND and OR can all be built from NAND gates alone (NOT A = A NAND A, etc.), and every Boolean function can be built from NOT, AND and OR, so any circuit can be made from NANDs only – simplifying manufacture. items.stem: Give one argument for and one argument against this view: "Building circuits only from NAND gates is always the best design choice."
items.answer: Excellent for mass production of chips, but not always optimal in gate count or clarity.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: a single gate type simplifies manufacture and reduces cost; NAND is fast in CMOS technology. Arguments against: may need more gates than a mixed design, increasing delay; harder for humans to read and debug. Supported judgement: Excellent for mass production of chips, but not always optimal in gate count or clarity.

items.stem: A half adder adds two bits A and B to give a sum S and a carry C. Construct its truth table, derive Boolean expressions for S and C, and explain how two half adders and an OR gate form a full adder.
items.answer: Truth table: 00→S0C0, 01→S1C0, 10→S1C0, 11→S0C1. S = A XOR B, C = A AND B. Full adder: first half adder adds A and B; second adds the result to Cin giving the final sum; the carry out is the OR of the two half-adder carries.
items.markingKey: Truth table: 00→S0C0, 01→S1C0, 10→S1C0, 11→S0C1. S = A XOR B, C = A AND B. Full adder: first half adder adds A and B; second adds the result to Cin giving the final sum; the carry out is the OR of the two half-adder carries.

items.stem: Explain why a truth table for n inputs has 2^n rows.
items.answer: Each input can independently be 0 or 1, so the number of combinations doubles with each additional input: 2 × 2 × … = 2^n.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Each input can independently be 0 or 1, so the number of combinations doubles with each additional input: 2 × 2 × … = 2^n. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.answer: NAND is 0 only for all-1 inputs; NOR is 1 only for all-0 inputs – the tables are different.

items.stem: Explain why brackets are important when writing a Boolean expression from a problem description.
items.answer: AND is usually evaluated before OR, so without brackets "A AND B OR C" means (A AND B) OR C; brackets ensure the expression matches the intended conditions, otherwise the circuit gives wrong outputs for some inputs.

items.answer: C AND P AND NOT W

items.stem: A group of four 1s in a 4-variable K-map eliminates how many variables?

items.stem: Briefly explain why grouping adjacent 1s in a K-map simplifies an expression.
items.answer: Adjacent cells differ in exactly one variable, so within a group that variable appears both as 1 and 0 and cancels (X·Y + X·NOT Y = X); larger groups cancel more variables, giving fewer gates.

items.markingKey: Correct K-map with 1s in cells 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 (1 mark); correct groups (1-2 marks); F = A OR (C AND NOT B) (1 mark). Any equivalent minimal SOP is accepted.

items.stem: Explain the difference between NOT (A OR B) and NOT A OR NOT B.
items.answer: NOT (A OR B) is 1 only when both are 0 (equal to NOT A AND NOT B); NOT A OR NOT B is 1 unless both are 1 (equal to NOT (A AND B)).
items.markingKey: NOT (A OR B) is 1 only when both are 0 (equal to NOT A AND NOT B); NOT A OR NOT B is 1 unless both are 1 (equal to NOT (A AND B)). One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): K-map rows are labelled in normal binary order.
Reason (R): Adjacent cells must differ in only one variable.
Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
items.answer: A is false but R is true.
items.markingKey: D. A false (Gray code is used); R true – which is why.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a bit and a byte.
items.answer: A bit is a single binary digit; a byte is a group of 8 bits, the usual unit for addressing memory and measuring file size.
items.markingKey: A bit is a single binary digit; a byte is a group of 8 bits, the usual unit for addressing memory and measuring file size. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem:

Reason (R): XOR is used to compute the sum bit in a half adder.
Which option is correct?
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
items.answer: A is false but R is true.
items.markingKey: D. A false (XOR gives 0 for 1,1); R true.

items.stem: Explain how a truth table can be used to check that a circuit matches a specification.
items.answer: Every input combination is listed and the output of the circuit is calculated for each and compared with the required output; if all rows match the circuit is correct, because a combinational circuit's behaviour is completely described by its truth table.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Every input combination is listed and the output of the circuit is calculated for each and compared with the required output; if all rows match the circuit is correct, because a combinational circuit's behaviour is completely described by its truth table. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A student claims: "In a K-map you may group three adjacent 1s." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Groups must contain a power of two cells; three 1s need two overlapping groups of two.
items.markingKey: Groups must contain a power of two cells; three 1s need two overlapping groups of two. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Represent -8 in 8-bit two's complement. Show your working.

options: XOR
NAND
AND
XNOR
items.answer: XNOR
items.markingKey: D. XNOR gives 1 0 0 1.

items.stem: A game sprite sheet is 1920 × 1080 pixels with a colour depth of 4 bits. Calculate the file size in KiB, ignoring metadata.

A logic circuit is described gate by gate: G1 is a NOT gate with input B; G2 is a OR gate with inputs C and G1; G3 is a XOR gate with inputs A and C; G4 is a OR gate with inputs G2 and G3. The output X is taken from G4. Write a Boolean expression for X and find X when A = 1, B = 0, C = 1.
items.answer: X = (C OR NOT B) OR (A XOR C); X = 1
items.markingKey: X = (C OR NOT B) OR (A XOR C) (2 marks, 1 for partial); value 1 (1 mark).

items.stem: Write X = (B NAND A) XOR (NOT (NOT C XOR A)) as a sum of minterms (canonical sum of products), giving the minterm numbers.
items.answer: m(0, 2, 5, 6): (NOT A AND NOT B AND NOT C) OR (NOT A AND B AND NOT C) OR (A AND NOT B AND C) OR (A AND B AND NOT C)
items.markingKey: Truth table rows with X = 1: 0, 2, 5, 6 (1-2 marks); correct minterms (1 mark).

items.stem: Diego writes: "In two's complement, 10000000 represents −0." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Two's complement has only one zero; 10000000 represents −128.
items.markingKey: Two's complement has only one zero; 10000000 represents −128. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Case study context: Banco Andino, a savings bank in Quito, runs an online banking website, issues mobile apps to customers and encrypts all transactions.
(a) Hana writes: "NAND and NOR give the same truth table because both start with N." Explain why this is inaccurate. Refer to Banco Andino in your answer. [3]
(b) Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Building circuits only from NAND gates is always the best design choice." Refer to Banco Andino in your answer. [3]
items.answer: (a) NAND is 0 only for all-1 inputs; NOR is 1 only for all-0 inputs – the tables are different. (b) Excellent for mass production of chips, but not always optimal in gate count or clarity.
items.markingKey: (a) [3 marks] NAND is 0 only for all-1 inputs; NOR is 1 only for all-0 inputs – the tables are different. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (b) [3 marks] Arguments for: a single gate type simplifies manufacture and reduces cost; NAND is fast in CMOS technology. Arguments against: may need more gates than a mixed design, increasing delay; harder for humans to read and debug. Supported judgement: Excellent for mass production of chips, but not always optimal in gate count or clarity. Credit is given only for points applied to the stated organisation (not generic answers).

items.stem: A museum in Seoul wants to digitise 2000 photographs and 300 hours of oral-history audio. Calculate example storage requirements for chosen settings, and discuss how resolution, colour depth, sample rate and bit depth should be chosen to balance quality and storage.
items.answer: e.g. photos 4000×3000 × 24 bits = 36 MB each → 72 GB; audio 44.1 kHz × 16 bits × 1 channel = 88.2 kB/s → 300 h ≈ 95 GB. Higher settings preserve detail for archive (lossless TIFF/FLAC), lower settings or lossy compression suffice for web access copies. Speech needs less sample rate than music (e.g. 22 kHz).

items.stem:
Case study context: Danube Robotics, a manufacturer in Budapest, builds warehouse robots that use sensors, feedback control and on-board processors, and sends telemetry over 5G.
(a) Kwame writes: "Two circuits with different gates must have different truth tables." Explain why this is inaccurate. Refer to Danube Robotics in your answer. [2]
(b) Evaluate the claim: "Truth tables are the best way to verify a logic circuit." Refer to Danube Robotics in your answer. [4]
items.answer: (a) Different circuits can be logically equivalent (e.g. a NAND-only version of an OR circuit) and have identical truth tables. (b) Ideal for small circuits; algebra, K-maps or automated tools are needed for larger ones.
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] Different circuits can be logically equivalent (e.g. a NAND-only version of an OR circuit) and have identical truth tables. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation. (b) [4 marks] Arguments for: exhaustive – every input combination is checked; simple and mechanical. Arguments against: grows as 2^n rows, impractical for many inputs; gives no insight into how to simplify the circuit. Supported judgement: Ideal for small circuits; algebra, K-maps or automated tools are needed for larger ones. items.stem: A 3-input function F(A, B, C) is 1 for the input combinations 001, 011, 101 and 111. Draw a K-map, simplify F, and prove the result with Boolean algebra.
items.answer: All four 1s lie where C = 1, forming one group of four: F = C. Algebra: F = A'B'C + A'BC + AB'C + ABC = A'C(B' + B) + AC(B' + B) = A'C + AC = C(A' + A) = C.
items.markingKey: All four 1s lie where C = 1, forming one group of four: F = C. Algebra: F = A'B'C + A'BC + AB'C + ABC = A'C(B' + B) + AC(B' + B) = A'C + AC = C(A' + A) = C.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "overflow"?
options: An error that occurs when the result of a calculation is too large to be stored in the available number of bits
A logic circuit whose output depends only on its current inputs, with no memory of previous inputs
The smallest addressable element of a bitmap image, which has one colour
A gate whose output is 0 only when all inputs are 1 – the inverse of AND; any circuit can be built from NAND gates alone
items.answer: An error that occurs when the result of a calculation is too large to be stored in the available number of bits
items.markingKey: A. "overflow" is an error that occurs when the result of a calculation is too large to be stored in the available number of bits.

items.stem: A student claims: "NOT (A AND B) is the same as NOT A AND NOT B." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a sum-of-products expression and a minterm.
items.answer: A minterm is one AND term covering exactly one input row with all variables present; an SOP is an OR of AND terms, which may be minterms or simplified products.
items.markingKey: A minterm is one AND term covering exactly one input row with all variables present; an SOP is an OR of AND terms, which may be minterms or simplified products. items.stem: Distinguish between two's complement and unsigned binary.
items.answer: Unsigned binary treats every bit as positive, so 8 bits give 0-255; two's complement gives the MSB a negative weight (−128), so 8 bits give −128 to +127 and allow negative numbers.
items.markingKey: Unsigned binary treats every bit as positive, so 8 bits give 0-255; two's complement gives the MSB a negative weight (−128), so 8 bits give −128 to +127 and allow negative numbers. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.answer: That describes XOR; OR outputs 1 when at least one input is 1, including when both are 1.

items.answer: A Boolean expression is the algebraic description of a function; a logic circuit is the physical arrangement of gates that implements it. Each can be derived from the other.

items.stem:
(a) State what is meant by the term "binary". [2]
(b) Briefly explain why computers use binary to represent data. [2]
(c) Ingrid writes: "Hexadecimal saves memory because it uses fewer digits than binary." Explain why this is inaccurate. [3]

items.stem:
Case study context: PixelForge, a games studio in Montreal, renders 3D scenes on GPU workstations, keeps large asset files on a NAS and collaborates with freelancers around the world.
(a) Explain the difference between bit depth and sample rate. Refer to PixelForge in your answer. [2]
(b) "UTF-8 is the best choice of encoding for every text file." To what extent is this view justified? Refer to PixelForge in your answer. [4]
items.answer: (a) Sample rate is how many samples are taken per second; bit depth is how many bits store each sample's amplitude. (b) UTF-8 is the best default for interoperability, though UTF-16 can be more compact for some scripts.
items.markingKey: (a) [2 marks] Sample rate is how many samples are taken per second; bit depth is how many bits store each sample's amplitude. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions). (b) [4 marks] Arguments for: backward compatible with ASCII and uses 1 byte for English text; can represent every Unicode character; the web standard. Arguments against: East Asian text needs 3 bytes per character, larger than UTF-16; variable length makes indexing the n-th character slower. Supported judgement: UTF-8 is the best default for interoperability, though UTF-16 can be more compact for some scripts. items.stem: A greenhouse vent V must open if the temperature is high (T) and it is not raining (R), or if humidity is high (H) regardless of the rain. Write a Boolean expression for V, construct its truth table and describe a logic circuit that implements it.
items.answer: V = (T AND NOT R) OR H. Truth table (T,R,H → V): 000→0, 001→1, 010→0, 011→1, 100→1, 101→1, 110→0, 111→1. Circuit: NOT gate on R, AND gate with T and NOT R, OR gate combining that output with H.
items.markingKey: V = (T AND NOT R) OR H. Truth table (T,R,H → V): 000→0, 001→1, 010→0, 011→1, 100→1, 101→1, 110→0, 111→1. Circuit: NOT gate on R, AND gate with T and NOT R, OR gate combining that output with H.

items.stem: "K-maps are the most effective method for simplifying logic expressions." To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: Best for small hand-designed circuits; algorithmic tools are better for real chip design.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: visual, quick and reliable for up to four variables; easy to spot don't-care conditions. Arguments against: impractical beyond five or six variables; software tools (Quine-McCluskey, Espresso) scale better. Supported judgement: Best for small hand-designed circuits; algorithmic tools are better for real chip design.
